summary.intent: Fix all four review findings on PR #267 and survey the codebase for the same patterns. Then resolve the open items (Chakra investigation, harness fixes, stacked PRs in Entire) using parallel agent teams and workflows.
summary.outcome: All four findings were fixed with tests that fail on old code and pass on new, and opened as draft PR #270 because #267 had already merged. The layer-members PR #271 was opened and linked to trail 125; linking trail 127 hit a 409, and the parallel workflow (wf_f39a3c3f-294) was still running.

repo: Component extractor and resolver code lives in crates/core/src/extractor and crates/core/src/resolver; the core and semantic suites run via cargo nextest on caliper-docgen-core and caliper-docgen-semantic (792 tests).
Regression check compares component sets, detection rules and prop counts on Chakra (618) and Mantine (356) before and after a change.
The gh shim runs `gh pr create` as the bot so a human can approve; `gh pr edit`/`ready` run as the user, and Entire opens PRs under its own identity.
`entire trail link` opens its own draft PR, so linking after `gh pr create` risks duplicate PRs. Linking a change already tied to another trail returns a 409.
Entire Gates requires a human approval per trail; the agent cannot approve trails.
A guard blocks shell commands whose text matches the bot's name, including history searches.
Alias handling in the resolver should use exhaustive matches over every alias variant so new variants fail to compile rather than being skipped.
Type-level matching (`try_fc_annotation`, `super_class_is_component_family`) matches names like FC and Component without checking the import source, the same flaw fixed for calls.

code.finding: Reads React's own aliases and handles only Intersection and Passthrough (at 83-87 and 128-132); a candidate for the alias-variant gap, though it looks correct for React's declarations.
Same alias-variant handling shape as html.rs; flagged as a candidate for the wildcard-match gap but left unchanged.
Fixed a panic where `memo(forwardRef<HTMLDivElement>())` indexed a missing second type argument, and made foreign-imported `forwardRef<Ref, Props>` keep detection and `ref`.

Tagged factories are now promoted after all other candidates, so `Group = withContext<..., GroupProps>(StyledGroup)` claims GroupProps before the private factory; alias shape evidence now reads Omit, Pick, Partial, Required and unions.

workflow: To confirm new tests catch the bugs, save the fix as a patch, restore the old code, run the tests (exactly the four new ones fail), then reapply the patch.
Long multi-command shell lines and inline edits were split into script files plus plain runs to keep them manageable.
Scout inline first, then run Workflow for parallel independent streams, with an independent review of each branch.
Confirm a PR's merge state before pushing fixes to it; a fresh branch and new PR is the fallback when it already merged.

friction: PR #267 merged just before the review finished, so the fixes needed a new branch and PR #270.
Entire Gates approval cannot be done by the agent and blocks merging #268 and the other PRs.
The trail 127 link returned a 409 because the change already belongs to another trail.
The guard blocked a history search because the query contained the bot's name.
A combined shell command for adding tests failed and had to be split into a script file and a plain run.
An empty probe workflow finished and produced a misleading completion notification while the real workflow was still running.
open_items: Resolve the 409 on linking trail 127 and decide whether #270 should be linked and marked ready.
Entire Gates approvals are still needed for #268, #270 and #271; planned merge order is #268, the layer branch, then a weekly re-run.

Wait for the pending parallel workflow (wf_f39a3c3f-294) results, then review the stacked-PR work and how Entire handles stacking.
Leave ADR 0022 unedited and keep current state in type-checker-integration.md.
